2607.27536.title: Strategy, Not Payoffs: A Behavioural Embedding of Normal-Form Games
2607.27536.paper_summary: Learning a strategic task changes more than what is directly taught: fine-tuning on one game can either enhance or degrade an agent's ability to reason in another. Understanding and predicting this transfer of strategic capabilities, however, remains a key challenge for large language models (LLMs). Normal-form games provide an ideal testbed for analyzing this phenomenon, as they feature explicitly defined payoffs and well-characterized equilibrium behaviours. In this work, we investigate whether game embeddings can explain and predict changes in LLM strategic capabilities following fine-tuning across different games. We propose a lightweight two-feature embedding that captures fundamental behavioural demands: the entropy of the Nash equilibrium and the sensitivity of optimal responses to an opponent's action. We show that while existing published structural embeddings primarily memorize game identities and fail to generalize, our behavioural embedding reliably predicts performance changes on held-out games. These results demonstrate that the transfer of strategic capabilities in LLMs is not dictated by the payoff geometry of a game, but by the underlying structure of the decision-making behaviour it requires.
2607.27536.paper_summary_zh: 學習一項策略任務改變的不僅僅是直接教授的內容：在一個遊戲上的微調可以增強或削弱代理在另一個遊戲中的推理能力。然後，理解和預測這種策略能力的轉移仍然是大型語言模型（LLMs）面臨的一個關鍵挑戰。常態形式遊戲為分析這一現象提供了理想的測試平台，因為它們具有明確定義的收益和良好特徵的均衡行為。在這項工作中，我們調查遊戲嵌入是否能解釋和預測在不同遊戲之間微調後LLM策略能力的變化。我們提出了一種輕量級的兩特徵嵌入，捕捉基本的行為需求：納什均衡的熵以及最佳反應對對手行動的敏感性。我們顯示，雖然現有的已發表結構嵌入主要記憶遊戲身份並且無法泛化，但我們的行為嵌入可靠地預測了在保留遊戲上的性能變化。這些結果顯示，LLMs中策略能力的轉移並不是由遊戲的收益幾何形狀決定的，而是由其所需的決策行為的基本結構決定的。
